The explanation about the treatment was minimal, and the reception staff were unhelpful. (They perform uninsured treatments without your knowledge.)
I will never use this clinic again.
Very good and nice dental clinic.

The dentist is Thai, but the pre-consultation(?) was done by a Japanese person, and there was an interpreter during treatment so communication was easy and I didn't feel anxious.
The price seems higher than at dentists in Japan, but considering that they also handle insurance and other matters overseas, it was totally reasonable.
I felt more at ease receiving treatment than when I previously received treatment at a general hospital.

As others have mentioned, it's simply expensive! And unlike in Japan, they explain the approximate cost of treatment... They start by telling you the minimum amount (cheap), but on the day it actually costs more than that. Also, every time they message me saying that their previous appointment was canceled, so if I'd like to come earlier... I'm worried about how they manage it.
The cost of root canal treatment for my back teeth is higher than the cost of implants I got at another local dentist! If that was the case, I would have chosen implants!

It's just so expensive. And am I the only one who feels like it's some kind of spiritual sales scam?
They said some pretty harsh things to me at my first consultation, and all the treatments are extremely expensive. On top of that, I don't even get 70% of the cost reimbursed from my Japanese company's social insurance.
Because it's way too expensive compared to 70% of the going rate in Japan, my out-of-pocket expenses are so high that it's really tough.
The only thing I sense is an aura that says, "They have interpreters and Japanese staff on-site, selling peace of mind. If you don't like it, you can just get treatment elsewhere." It's a scary atmosphere. I don't really feel like I'm safe now that I've started treatment at the hospital. I'm trembling at the thought of how much they'll charge me next time. And it's not just the cold and strong air in the examination room that's making me tremble. I'm in trouble.
If I don't get treated, it's going to be a big problem. But a month's salary would be gone in an instant. So I'll have to wait until I get treatment in Japan.
When I showed it to a Thai friend of mine, she said, "If it were me, I wouldn't get treatment. I'd just put up with it." If it's just a tooth extraction, I'll go to a local dentist.

There are a lot of mothers with children, and even though it's expensive, they keep quiet and pay, using their children's treatment as a hostage, so perhaps the prices end up getting even more expensive?
Sorry for being so harsh.

I was a little worried before going, but everyone from the receptionist to the doctor and dental hygienist were very kind and polite. 
It may be more expensive than other dental clinics (according to blog and website information), but I'm satisfied all the same.
Everyone was very kind and it was great that there were Japanese staff on site too, which was helpful.
They are a very good dentist, providing courteous service.

A dental clinic run by a Japanese owner.

The dentist is Thai, but they bring in highly skilled dentists from Bangkok, so you can rest assured.

An interpreter is also available.

I used their services for teeth cleaning and whitening!

The interpreter provides explanations and translations in Japanese, which is reassuring. They have specialists for tooth extraction, orthodontics, and cavity treatment, and although the prices are a bit higher, the equipment and tools are clean, so you can entrust your care to them with confidence. When I had a bad experience at another clinic, they provided a free diagnosis and attentive follow-up, which was incredibly helpful.

The two interpreters (male and female) clearly lacked Japanese language skills. They didn't even translate half of what the doctor said. They probably couldn't. I was very worried about whether the doctor fully understood what I was saying. …
